exemplar.title: What strong work looks like
exemplar.intro: Strong shop-owner work shows every percent step — here is how one student priced a bake-sale table.

traits.trait: Shows the percent as a computation
traits.sample: My brownies cost $0.80 to make. A 50% markup adds $0.40, so I sell them for $1.20 — I wrote 0.50 × 0.80 to prove it.
traits.why: The percent is turned into an equation, not just a final price.

traits.sample: At an 8% tax rate, a $2.50 cookie adds $0.20 tax because 0.08 × 2.50 = 0.20, making the total $2.70.
traits.why: It shows the decimal multiplication and states what the answer means.

traits.sample: A 25% discount on $4.00 saves more than $0.75 off, because 25% is $1.00 — so I advertised the percent deal.
traits.why: Two offers are converted to dollars so the comparison is fair.

traits.trait: Connects math to the business choice
traits.sample: I priced lemon bars at $1.50 instead of $2.00 because my table shows I sell twice as many, which earns more overall.
traits.why: The numbers drive the decision — that is what the top rubric row asks for.
